validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of prevention strategies for urologic tumors summarizing existing evidence rather than presenting original human study data on Mediterranean diet and prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Food groups and risk of prostate cancer: a case-control study in Uruguay.
validated_results.reason: Original case-control study reporting a dairy (whole milk) intake odds ratio for incident, microscopically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma.

extraction.timing: Incident cases with exposure assessed prior to diagnosis via dietary questionnaire (not explicitly detailed)
extraction.population: Men with incident microscopically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma and hospital-based controls

sample_size.excerpt: Data were derived from 326 cases with incident and microscopically confirmed adenocarcinomas of the prostate and 652 controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 326 + 652 = 978

cases.excerpt: Data were derived from 326 cases with incident and microscopically confirmed adenocarcinomas of the prostate and 652 controls.

effect_size.excerpt: We identified the following food items as risk factors: lamb meat, salted meat, whole milk, total eggs, and maté consumption. The highest OR was associated with total eggs (OR, 2.43; 95 % CI, 1.70-3.48), followed by salted meat (OR, 2.65; 95 % CI, 1.36-3.76), maté consumption (OR, 1.96; 95 % CI, 1.17-3.31), and whole milk (OR, 2.01; 95 % CI, 1.26-2.51).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The highest OR was associated with total eggs (OR, 2.43; 95 % CI, 1.70-3.48), followed by salted meat (OR, 2.65; 95 % CI, 1.36-3.76), maté consumption (OR, 1.96; 95 % CI, 1.17-3.31), and whole milk (OR, 2.01; 95 % CI, 1.26-2.51).

comparison.excerpt: Odds ratios and 95 % confidence intervals of prostate cancer were estimated by unconditional multiple logistic regression.
